messages:
Asha Reddy: hi team, day 1 kube issue. I can `kubectl get pods -n dev` but `kubectl exec -it pod-name -n dev -- /bin/sh` fails with Forbidden. using Windows 11 + Git Bash. any quick tips? /cc @DevEx

DevEx: welcome Asha! can you paste the exact error and `kubectl config current-context`? also did you follow the SSO quickstart or a service-account kubeconfig?

Asha Reddy: current-context: redwood-dev. error:
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods "pod-name" is forbidden: User "user:asha@redwood.com" cannot create resource "pods/exec" in API group "" in the namespace "dev"
```
I used Okta SSO via the quickstart script.

DevEx: thanks — port-forward and exec are often gated. run `kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec -n dev` and `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n dev` to confirm.

Asha Reddy: `kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec -n dev` -> "no"
`kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n dev` -> "no"

InfraOps: sounds like you're in a read/view group only. canonical fix: People Ops add you to `redwood:team-dev` or the team that owns `dev`. Short-term: infra can apply a Role that includes the subresource verbs and bind it to your user. Example Role + RoleBinding we use for temp access:
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: dev-debug
  namespace: dev
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "pods/exec", "pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "create", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-asha-debug
  namespace: dev
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: "user:asha@redwood.com"
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: dev-debug
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
We revoke temp bindings once Okta group is synced. Want us to apply it?

Asha Reddy: yes please, would be great. also on Windows Git Bash I sometimes see kubeconfig with CRLF diffs — could that break token parsing?

DevEx: good question. CRLF can corrupt OIDC token files if you manual-edit kubeconfig. Avoid editing tokens by hand; use the quickstart script to regenerate the kubeconfig. If you suspect CRLF issues run `dos2unix ~/.kube/config` or use Windows `wsl` to fetch a clean kubeconfig. We'll add a note to the docs.

Onboard Bot: access request 9122 created -> awaiting infra temp-binding if requested.

InfraOps: applied onboarding-asha-debug in dev (auto-revoke in 12h). Try the exec now.

Asha Reddy: confirmed! `kubectl exec -it pod-name -n dev -- /bin/sh` now opens a shell. thanks!! :tada:

People Ops: following up to add Asha to `redwood:team-dev` in Okta so we can remove the temp binding. expect group sync within 24h.

DevEx: noted about CRLF/kubeconfig on Windows — we'll add a small troubleshooting section in the quickstart recommending `dos2unix`, WSL usage, and the `kubectl auth can-i` checks for exec/portforward. PR incoming. :thumbsup:
